x: The people of interpretation differed regarding his saying Qaf.
Some of them said: It is one of the names of God Almighty, by which He swore.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Dawud told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Qaf, Nun, and similar words, for it is an oath that God has sworn, and it is one of the names of God.

x: Others said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, Qaf, he said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an.

x: Others said: Qaf is the name of the mountain surrounding the earth. Our explanation of the interpretation of the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of the chapters of the Qur’an has been presented before, sufficiently so that we do not need to repeat it here. And his saying,
h
And the Glorious Qur’an
, means: And the Noble Qur’an.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’ar bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr:
m: “Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an.” He said: The Noble Qur’an. The Arabists differed about the position of the answer to this oath.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said, Qaf, by the Glorious Qur’an, is an oath based on His statement, We know what the earth takes away from them.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said, It contains the meaning by which He swore. He said, He mentioned that it was decreed by God. He said, “It is said that Qaf is a mountain surrounding the earth. If that is the case, then it is as if it is in the nominative case: that is, it is Qaf, by God.” He said, “Its nominative case should have been made clear because it is a noun and not a spelling.

i: He said, “Perhaps Qaf alone was mentioned in its noun, as the poet said:
x: I told her to stand for us, she said stand The letter Qaf was mentioned to indicate that Qaf is from the word “stop”, meaning that I am standing.

This statement is, in our view, the more correct of the two statements, because the word qad is not known in the answers to oaths. Rather, oaths are answered if they are answered with one of the four letters: lam, “in,” ma, and la, or if their answer is omitted, then it is invalid.

And His statement, Rather, they were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, "O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people did not lie to you, because they did not know that you were truthful and just, but they lied to you out of amazement that a warner had come to them warning them of God's punishment from among them, meaning a human being from among the children of Adam, and that no angel had come to them with a message from God." And His statement,
h
Then the disbelievers said

, ‘This is an amazing thing.’ God Almighty says: The disbelievers from among the Quraysh said when a warner came to them from among themselves, This is an amazing thing. That is, the coming of a man from among us from among Adam with God’s message to us, Why was an angel not sent down to him to be with him as a warner?

The speaker says: The resurrection was not mentioned, so he tells about these people’s disbelief in what they called for, so what is the point of reporting about them that they denied what they did not call for, and their response to what they were not asked about? It was said: The Arab scholars differed on this, so we will mention what they said on this, then we will follow it with the explanation, God willing. One of the grammarians of Basra said about this: If we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? He did not mention that he returned, and that, and God knows best, was in response, as if it was said to them: You will return, so they said: If we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? And one of the grammarians of Kufa said: His statement:
h
If we die and become dust is a statement before which it was not clear what this could be an answer to
, but its meaning is implied, and God knows best: “Qaf.

By the Glorious Qur’an” You will be resurrected after death, so they said: If we are dust, will we be resurrected? They denied the resurrection, then said, That is a far-fetched return. They denied it entirely, and his saying, far-fetched, is like saying to a man who makes a mistake in a matter: You have gone a long way from the truth, meaning you have made a mistake. And the correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that in this speech there is something omitted and the evidence of what was mentioned is sufficient to support its mention. That is because God indicated with His report of the denial of these polytheists, with whom He began this surah with the report of their denial of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with His saying, “Rather, they are amazed that a warner has come to them from among themselves. So the disbelievers say, ‘This is an amazing thing,’” His threat to them for their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is as if He said to them, if they say, denying the message of God, His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, This is an amazing thing, you will know, O people, when you are resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, what your state will be in your denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and your denial of his prophethood.
So they said, responding to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
When we die and become dust

, we know that, and we see what you promised us for your denial. That is a far-fetched return, meaning that that will not happen, and we will not return alive after our death. So He was sufficient with the evidence of His saying, Rather, they are amazed that A warner came to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers said, “This is an amazing thing.
And in what was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, he said: I heard Abu Muadh say:

c: Ubaid told us:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
When we die and become dust

, is that a far-fetched return? They said: How can God protect you when we have become bones and dust, and have wandered in the earth? This is evidence of the truth of what we said, that they denied the resurrection when they were threatened with it.

x: And His statement,
h
We know what the earth takes from them

, God Almighty says: We know what the earth consumes of their bodies after their death, what the earth consumes and destroys of their bodies, and they have a written record, along with Our knowledge of that, preserving all of that. God Almighty called it the Preserver, because what is written in it does not fade away, nor does it change or alter. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement,
h
We know what the earth takes away from them
, means: What the earth consumes of their flesh, skin, bones, and hair.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
What the earth diminishes of them
, he said: Of their bones.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
We know what the earth takes away from them
, meaning: what the earth consumes from them.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
We know what the earth takes away from them
. He said: It means death. He said: Who among them dies, or he said: What the earth consumes from them when they die.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: God said, We know what the earth takes of them, meaning: what the earth consumes of them, and we know about it, and they are with me, along with my knowledge of them, in a preserved book.

x: God Almighty says: What happened to these polytheists who said, When we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? in their saying this? Rather, they denied the truth, which is the Qur’an, when it came to them from God.

c: Like what Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, meaning they denied the truth when it came to them, meaning they denied the Qur’an.
h
So they are in a confused matter

, he says: They are in a confused and ambiguous matter, they do not know what is right from what is wrong. It is said that the matter of the people has become confused if it is mixed up and neglected. The interpretation of the verse has been interpreted differently by the commentators, although they have similar meanings.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: They are in a reprehensible matter. He said: Al-Marij is the reprehensible thing.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash told me: Salma bin Qutaybah told me, on the authority of Wahb bin Habib Al-Amidi, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he was asked about his statement, A disturbing matter. He said: Disturbing is the reprehensible thing. Haven’t you heard the poet say: Suddenly, she sought him with her innermost being, and he became proud like a thread of silk.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: in a different matter.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, in a matter of doubt, meaning: different.

x: Others said: Rather, it means: in a matter of misguidance.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
They are in a confused matter
. He said: He said: They are in a matter of misguidance.

x: Others said: Rather, it means: in an ambiguous matter.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So they are in a confused matter
, he said: Confused.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
A confused matter
, he said: Ambiguous.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
They are in a confused matter
, meaning that the matter is unclear to them.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, who said:
m: His religion became confusing to him.

x: Others said: Rather, it is mixed.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement, in
h
a confused matter

, he said: Confused means mixed. I said: Although these expressions differ in wording, they are similar in meaning, because something is different and ambiguous, and its meaning is problematic. If it is like that, it is reprehensible, because what is known is clear and obvious. If it is unknown, then it is undoubtedly misguidance, because guidance is clear and unambiguous.

x: And His statement,
h
Have they not looked at the sky above them

, how We constructed it? God Almighty says: Have these deniers of resurrection after death, who deny Our ability to revive them after their affliction, not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it? So We proportioned it as a protected ceiling, and adorned it with stars. “
h
And it has no rifts
.” Meaning: It has no cracks or fissures. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, of the clefts, he said: split.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And it has no rifts
. I said to him, meaning Ibn Zayd: Are rifts something that is disassociated from one another? He said: Yes.

x: And His statement,
h
And the earth We have spread out
, meaning:
h
And the earth We have spread out
h
And We cast therein firm mountains

, meaning: And We placed therein firm mountains, firmly planted in the earth. And We caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind, meaning: And We caused to grow in the earth of every kind of beautiful plant, which is the beautiful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Bahij meaning: beautiful.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And We cast therein firm mountains
, and firm mountains are mountains, and We caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind, meaning of every beautiful kind.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: I said to Ibn Zayd al-Bahij: Is it good looking? He said: Yes.

x: And His statement, As insight, means: We did that as insight for you, O people, so that He may make you aware of your Lord’s power over whatever He wills. And a reminder for every servant who turns back, means: And a reminder from God of His greatness and power, and an alert to His Oneness. For every servant who turns back, means: For every servant who returns to faith in God and acts in obedience to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, insight: a blessing from God that the servants see. And a reminder for every servant who turns in repentance: meaning one who turns with his heart to God.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Insight and Reminder
, he said: Insight from God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, insight, he said: insight.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’ and Mujahid:
m: For every servant who turns back. They said: One who responds.

x: God Almighty says, And We sent down water from the sky, blessed rain, and with it We caused orchards of trees to grow, and the harvested grain of wheat, barley, and all kinds of grains.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the grain of the harvest
means wheat and barley.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the grain of the harvest
He said: It is wheat and barley.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And the grain of the harvest
he said: wheat. Some Arab scholars used to say in his statement,
h
And the grain of the harvest
, that the grain is the harvest, and it is one of the things that is attributed to itself, like his statement, Indeed, this is the absolute truth (al-Waqi’ah 56:95).

x: And his saying,
h
And tall palm trees

, means: And We caused to grow, with the water which We sent down from the sky, tall palm trees. Tall means tall. A tall mountain is called a tall mountain, as Abu Nawfal said to Abu Hubayrah: O son of those who, by their grace, brought the river to Qais Fazara And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, tall, meaning tall.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement,
h
And the tall palm trees
, he said: Tall palm trees.

c: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the tall palm trees
, he said: In their trunks means their height in standing.

c: Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And tall palm trees
. Tall means tall.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, tall and tall. He said: tall.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the tall palm trees
. He said: With their stems, their height.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the tall palm trees
. He said: It means their height.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
and tall palm trees

, that tall means tall. His saying, Its dates are arranged in layers, means: This tall palm tree has dates, which are the Kafranbel. Arranged: he says: arranged one on top of the other, overlapping. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: It has a date palm in layers. He said: He says one part on top of the other.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Nadid, he said: Arranged.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It has a cluster of dates. He said: Some of it is on top of others.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: It has a date palm in layers meaning it is arranged one on top of the other.

x: And His statement, provision for the servants, means: We created with this water that We sent down from the sky these gardens, the grain and the palm trees as sustenance for the servants, some of it as food, and some of it as fruit and enjoyment. And His statement,
h
And We revived thereby a dead land
, God Almighty says,
h
And We revived thereby a dead land

that had become barren and dry, with no plants or vegetation. And His statement, Likewise is the emergence, God Almighty says: Just as We caused this dead land to grow with this water, and revived it with it, and brought forth its plants and its crops, thus We will bring you forth on the Day of Resurrection alive from your graves after your affliction in them with what descends upon it of water.

God Almighty says, You have denied before these polytheists who denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his people, the people of Noah and the companions of the Messenger. We have already mentioned before the matter of the companions of the Messenger, and that they were a people who threw their prophet into a well.

m: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Ikrimah on the same authority.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The Companions of Al-Rass, and Al-Rass is a well in which the companion of Yasin was killed.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The Companions of the Well, he said: A well.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Amr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The people of the thicket - the thicket means the destroyed trees - and the people of the tree were two nations. Then God sent to them one prophet, Shuʿayb, and God punished them with two punishments: And Thamud, and ʿAd, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot, and the people of the thicket, who were the people of Shuʿayb, and their story has already passed, and the people of Tubba’. The people of Tubba were idolaters.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq.
m: His story and the story of his people were as follows:

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Imran bin Hudayr told us on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he asked Abdullah bin Salam, what was Tubba’? He said: Tubba’ was a man from the Arabs, and he gained power over the people, so he chose young men from the best, and kept them company and brought them in, until he took from them and pledged allegiance to them. His people were arrogant about that and said: He has abandoned your religion and pledged allegiance to the young men. When that became widespread, he said to the young men, and the young men said: Between us and them is the fire, which burns the liar and saves the truthful from it. So they did, and the young men hung their copies of the Qur’an around their necks, then they went to the fire, and when they were about to enter it, the fire scorched their faces, so they turned back from it. Tubba’ said to them: You must enter it. So when they entered it, it opened up to them until they cut it open. And he said to his al-Nas 114:Enter it. So when they were about to enter it, the fire scorched their faces, so they turned back from it. Tubba’ said to him: You must enter it. So when they entered it, it opened up to them, until when they reached the middle, it surrounded them and burned them. So Tubba’ became a Muslim, and Tubba’ was a righteous man.
b.via: Abu Majlaz on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Malik bin Tha’labah bin Abi Malik Al-Qurazi, who said:
m: I heard Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Qurazi, who said: I heard Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Talha bin Abdullah narrating that when Tubba’ approached Yemen to enter it, Himyar prevented him from doing so and said: Do not enter it upon us, for you have abandoned our religion. So he called them to his religion and said: It is a religion better than your religion. They said: Then judge us by the Fire! He said: Yes. He said: And in Yemen, as the people of Yemen claim, there was a fire that judged between them in what they differed about, devouring the oppressor and not harming the oppressed. When they said that to Tubba’, he said: You have been fair. So his people went out with their idols and what they used to draw near to God in their religion. He said: And the two rabbis went out with their copies of the Qur’an around their necks, wearing them with chains of mail, until they sat for the fire at the exit from which it emerged. Then the fire came out to them, and when it approached them, they turned away from it and feared it. So they threw stones at those who were present among the people and ordered them to be patient with it. So they were patient until it covered them and devoured the idols and what they had drawn near to God with it, and some of the men of Himyar. Then the two rabbis went out with their copies of the Qur’an around their necks, and the sweat on their foreheads did not harm them. Then Himyar adhered to its religion. From there and other than that, the origin of Judaism was in Yemen. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of some of his companions that the two rabbis and those who went out with them from Himyar only followed the fire to destroy it, and they said: Whoever destroys it is more deserving of the right. So some men from Himyar approached them with their idols to destroy it, but it approached them to consume them, but they turned away and were unable to destroy it. The two rabbis
b.via: Abu Malik bin Tha’labah bin Abi Malik Al-Qurazi

x: God Almighty said: And Aad, Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot.
And the Almighty said: And the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubba’ - all denied the messengers, so my threat came true.

This is a rebuke from God to the polytheists of Quraysh who said: If we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? God, the Most High, says to them: We were exhausted by inventing the first creation which We created when it was nothing, so we are exhausted by bringing them back as a new creation after they have decayed in the dust and perished. He says: That does not exhaust Us, rather We are able to do it. And we bark what we said in that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Are We tired with the first creation
? He said: The first creation did not tire us.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Are We weary with the first creation
? He said: Are We weary when We created you as a new creation, so you doubt the resurrection?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Maysarah:
m: h
Are We weary with the first creation

? He said: We created you. And His statement, Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation, God Almighty says: These polytheists who deny the resurrection do not doubt that We did not fail in the first creation, but they are in doubt about Our ability to create them a new creation after their annihilation and their trial in their graves. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation, meaning: in doubt about the resurrection.

c: Ibn Haimed told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Maysar:
m: Rather, they are in confusion. He said: The disbelievers. From a new creation. He said: That they will be created after death.

c: Bishr told us: Szsd told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Rather, they are in confusion: meaning, doubt - and the new creation: the resurrection after death - so people became two types of al-Nas 114:those who deny and those who believe.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
In confusion of a new creation
, he said: Resurrection after death.

m: that he had heard that if a man commits a sin, the scribe on the right says to the one on the left: Write. He says: No, you write. They both refuse, so a caller calls out: O scribe on the left, write what the scribe on the right omitted.

x: And in His statement,
h

The first is that the intoxication of death, which is its severity and its overwhelming power over man's understanding, like intoxication from sleep or drink, will come with the truth of the matter of the Hereafter, thus alerting man so that he may be certain of it and know it. The second is that the intoxication of death will come with the reality of death. It was mentioned about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, that he was reading and the intoxication of truth came with death.
The narration mentioned that:

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Wasil, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said:

Rather, it is as God the Almighty said: “And the intoxication of truth has come with death.
h
That is what you were avoiding

.” It has been mentioned that this is also the way Ibn Masʿud read it. There are two interpretations for the way in which someone reads it: One of them is: And the intoxication of God came with death, so the truth is God Almighty. The second is: That the intoxication is death, attributed to itself, as it was said: Indeed, this is the certain truth, so the interpretation of the statement is: And the true intoxication came with death. His saying,
h
That is what you were avoiding

m: The meaning of

h
Throw into Hell every obstinate disbeliever there is something omitted in it that is dispensed with by the apparent meaning of it

meaning. The second: That it is as some of the Arabs used to say, which is that the Arabs command one person and a group with what they command two people, so they say to the man, Woe to you, saddle it and drive it away. He mentioned that he heard it from the Arabs, and he said: And one of them recited to me: I said to my friend, Don’t detain us by uprooting its roots and cutting down its wormwood.

He said: Abu Tharwan recited to me: If you forbid me, O son of Affan, I will forbid, and if you call me, I will be an impregnable presence. He said: It is narrated that this is because a man has at least two helpers in his camels and sheep, and likewise the minimum number of companions is three. So the speech of one of them was directed towards his two companions, and he said: Don’t you see that poets are the most frequently spoken thing, my friend, my intimate friend? Imru' al-Qais said: My friend, I passed by Umm Jundub, and he broke the hearts of the tormented ones. Then he said: Didn't you see that whenever I came to a new place, I found it fragrant, even if it was not fragrant? So he returned to the one, and the first speech was two. He said: And some of them recited to me: My two friends, come to me while I am idle. See if you see any light from Dhu Abanin or from lightning.
Some of them say: We see light. Every stubborn disbeliever means: every stubborn denier of the oneness of God, and he is stubborn about the truth and the path of guidance.

c: Bishr told us that: Yazid told us that: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada.

We said that this is the correct statement, because God Almighty mentioned it in His statement preventing good that it prevents good and did not specify one thing over another, so this applies to every good that can be prevented by someone seeking it. His saying aggressive means: someone who is aggressive towards people with his tongue, with obscenities and vulgarity in speech, and with his hand, with force and oppression unjustly.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: that he was strict in his speech, his conduct, and his command. His saying doubtful means: doubting the oneness of God and His ability to do whatever He wills.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: who said: I said to Abu Al-ʿAliyah, Do not dispute in my presence, for I have already brought you the threat. Abu Jaʿfar Al-Tabari said: I think he said: They are the people of polytheism. And he said in another verse, Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord, so they are the people of the Qiblah.
b.via: Abu Jaʿfar on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what He will say to the polytheists and their jinn companions on the Day of Resurrection, when they will disavow each other: What will change the statement that I made to you in this world, which is His statement
h
I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together
, nor the judgment that I decreed for them therein?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
The word is not changed with Me
, I have decided what I am going to decide.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The word cannot be changed with Me
, he said: I have decided what I am going to decide. And His saying,
h
And I am not unjust to the servants
, means: I will not punish any of My creation for the crime of another, nor will I hold any of them responsible for a sin other than his own, and thus torment him for it.

x: And His statement,
h
On the Day We will say to Hell
, meaning: I will not be unjust to the servants
h
on the Day We will say to Hell

, Are you filled? That is on the Day of Resurrection. And the Day We will say is from the word of injustice. And the Most High said to Hell on the Day of Resurrection, Are you filled? because of His previous promise to it that He would fill it with jinn and people all together. As for his statement,
h
Is there any more
? the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: There is no more.

Rather, God says to it: Are you full after He places His foot in it, so some of it withdraws into some of it and says: Enough, enough, out of its constriction. Then when He says to it when it has become like this: Are you full? It then says:
h
Is there any more
Meaning: There is no more, because of its intense fullness and the constriction of some of it into some of it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
On the Day We will say to Hell

, ‘Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ Ibn Abbas said: God, the King, Blessed and Exalted be He, had previously said, I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together. So when the people were resurrected and brought forth, and the enemies of God were driven to the Fire in groups, they began to rush into Hell, group by group. Nothing was thrown into Hell but that it went into it, and nothing would fill it. It said, Did you not swear that you would fill me with jinn and people all together? Then he put his foot in it, and I said when he put his foot in it, It is done, for I am already filled, so I have no more. And nothing would fill it, until it felt the touch of what was placed on it, and it felt constricted when what was placed on it was placed, so it was filled with the space of a needle.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And she says, ‘Is there more?’ He said: God promised him that He would fill it, so he said, Why don’t I fulfill it for you? She said, Is there a way out?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
The Day We will say to Hell

, ‘Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ Ibn Ibn Abbas used to say: God, the Sovereign, had previously uttered a word from Him, I will surely fill Hell. Nothing will be thrown into it but will go into it, nothing will fill it, until not one of its people remains who will not have entered it, and nothing will fill it. Then the Lord will come to it and place His foot upon it, then say to it, ‘Are you filled, O Hell?’ It will say, ‘Enough, enough. I am filled. You have filled me with jinn and mankind, so there is no more.’ Ibn Abbas said: Nothing would fill it until it felt the touch of the foot of God, the Most High, and it became constricted, and there was not in it the space of a needle.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of increase me is is there more?, meaning to increase.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Thabit told us on the authority of Anas, who said:
m: He will be thrown into Hell and it will say: Is there more? three times, until he places his foot in it, and it will move away from one another, and it will say: Enough, enough, three times.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
On the Day We will say to Hell

, ‘Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ because it has been filled, and Are there any more? means, Is anyone left? He said: These are the two interpretations of this, and God knows best. He said: They said this and this. The first of the two opinions on this matter, in my opinion, is the correct one, which says: It means asking for more, is there anything I can add? We said that this is the more correct of the two sayings due to the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which says:

c: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam al-Ajli told me: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tafawi told us: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will not wrong any of His creation in the least, and he will be thrown into the Fire, which will say, ‘Is there more?’ until he places his foot on it. Then it will be filled, and some parts will be brought together, and it will say, ‘Enough, enough.’”

c: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam told us: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us:
m: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Anas who said: “Hell will continue to say: ‘Is there more?’ until God places His foot on it, and it will say: ‘Indeed, indeed.’

x: God Almighty means by His saying,
h
And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous

, not far away, that Paradise will be brought near and brought close to those who feared their Lord, so they feared His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous
, meaning: And it will be brought near, not far.

x: And His saying,
h
This is what you are promised
, means: He said to them:
h
This is what you are promised
, O righteous ones, that you will enter it and dwell in it. His saying,
h
For every penitent
means: for every person who returns from disobeying God to obeying Him, repenting from his sins. The commentators differed on the meaning of this.

Some of them said: It is the one who glorifies God, and some of them said: It is the one who repents. We have mentioned their differences on this in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. However, we will mention in this place what we did not mention there.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: For every one who turns back means for every one who glorifies God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muslim al-Awar, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Al-Awab is the one who glorifies God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Yahya bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Ghania told me: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah,
m: regarding the statement of God, For every one who turns back [to Him] and is mindful, he said: He is the one who remembers God in the privacy.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus bin Khabab, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
For every one who turns back [to God] is a guardian
. He said: The one who remembers his sins and seeks forgiveness for them.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
This is what you are promised to everyone who frequently turns back

. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Khajah, on the authority of Isa al-Hannat, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: He is the one who remembers his sins in private and seeks forgiveness for them. Hafiz means obedient to God and prays often.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
For every one who turns back [to God] is a guardian
, he said: The one who turns back [to God] is the one who turns back to God’s obedience and returns to it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Yunus bin Khabab,
m: regarding His statement,
h
For every one who turns back [to God]
, He is Preserver of [His] mercy. He said: The man remembers his sins and asks God for forgiveness for them. And his saying, Preserver, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: He preserved his sins until he repented from them.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about the repentant and the preserver. He said: He preserves his sins until he turns away from them.

x: Others said: It means that he is a guardian of God’s obligations and what He has entrusted him with.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Hafiz means: Hafiz is the guardian of what God has entrusted to him of His right and His blessings. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty described this repentant, returning person as a Guardian, and He did not specify that he guards one type of obedience over another. Rather, it should be general, as He, the Most High, is general. It should be said: He is a Guardian of everything that he brought to his Lord of the obligatory acts of obedience and the sins that he committed in the past, for which he repented and sought forgiveness.

x: And his saying:
h
Whoever fears the Most Merciful in secret

means: Whoever fears God in this world before meeting Him, obeys Him, and follows His command. As for min in his statement: Whoever fears, there are two ways of parsing: the accusative case is to follow kull in his statement: for every one who turns back, and the nominative case is to resume, and what is meant by it is the reward of whoever fears the Most Gracious in secret. It will be said to him: Enter Paradise. So then his statement: “Enter it in peace” is an answer to the reward, before which the statement was implied, and it was made an action for all, because min can be in the doctrine of all. His saying,
h
And he came with a heart repentant
, means: And he came to God with a heart repentant of his sins, turning from what God hates to what pleases Him.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he came with a heart turning in repentance
: meaning turning to his Lord and turning towards Him.

And His statement:
h
And during part of the night glorify Him
The people of interpretation differed regarding the glorification that He commanded during the night.
Some of them said: It means the Isha prayer.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And part of the night
, he said: darkness.

x: Others said: It is the night prayer at any time.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaid God bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And during a part of the night glorify Him. He said: During the entire night. Mujahid's statement on this matter is closer to being correct, because God, the Exalted, said:
h
And during part of the night glorify Him

. He did not specify a specific time during the night. If that is the case, then it applies to all hours of the night. If the matter is as we have described, then it is more like a command to pray the Maghrib and Isha prayers than a command to pray the Isha prayer, because they are both performed at night. His saying:
h
And at the end of prostration
means: Glorify your Lord with praise at the end of prostration in your prayer.

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning of the glorification that God commanded His Prophet to glorify Him after prostration.
Some of them said: It refers to prayer. They said: They are the two rak’ahs that are prayed after the Maghrib prayer.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, who said:
m: I asked Ali about the ends of prostration, and he said: The two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ali told us: Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: And the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Musʿab bin Salam told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, who said:
m: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: The ends of prostration are the two rakʿahs after the Maghrib prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement:
h
and the ends of prostration
, he said: The two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer. He said: Yahya told us:

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Asim bin Damrah, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ali,
m: may God be pleased with them both, who said: The ends of prostration are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer.

c: Ali bin Hilal told me: Muammil told us: Hammad told us: Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Aws bin Khalid, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: The two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alwan ibn Abi Malik, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: The ends of prostration are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The two rak’ahs after al-Sajdah 32:the number of rak’ahs of the Maghrib prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And during part of the night glorify Him
h
and at the end of prostration

and at the setting of the stars, he said: The two rakʿahs before dawn and the two rakʿahs after sunset. Shuʿbah said: I do not know which of them is prostration, and I do not know which of them is at the setting of the stars.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
and the ends of prostration
, he said: Mujahid used to say: Two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer.

c: Muhammad bin Saeed told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And the ends of prostration
, he said: They are the two prostrations after the Maghrib prayer. And during a part of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of prostration.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Fadil told us, on the authority of Rashdin bin Kurayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Ibn Abbas, two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer, after prostration.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam told me: Abu Zur’ah and Hibat God Rashid told us: Haywah bin Shureih told us: Abu Sakhr told us that
m: he heard Abu Mu’awiyah Al-Bajali from the people of Kufa say: I heard Abu Al-Sahbaa Al-Bakri say: I asked Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, about the ends of prostration. He said: They are two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer.

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me: Baqiyah told us: Jarir told us: Himyar bin Yazid Al-Rahbi told us on the authority of Krayb bin Yazid Al-Rahbi:
m: Jubayr bin Nufayr used to walk to him. He said: If he prayed the two rak’ahs before dawn and the two rak’ahs after sunset, he would make them shorter. He explained the setting of the stars and the ending of prostration.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: It was said: The ends of prostration are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. He said: Anbasa told us on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir on the authority of Mujahid: And the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. He said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Ata’ who said: Ali said: The two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us:
m: Al-Awza’i was asked about the two rak’ahs after Maghrib. He said: They are in the Book of God: So glorify Him and after prostration.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement:
h
And the ends of prostration
, he said: The two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the ends of prostration
he said: Two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying: and after prostration is the glorification of God after the obligatory prayers, not the prayer after them.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us on the authority of Mujahid: Ibn Abbas said
m: about So glorify Him and after al-Sajdah 32:It is the glorification after the prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn Amur told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, and at the ends of prostration, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: glorification. Ibn Amr said in his hadith: in all prayers. Al-Harith said in his hadith: at the end of all prayers.

x: Others said: They are the voluntary prayers after the obligatory prayers.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yunus bin Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: and the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the voluntary prayers. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The two rak’ahs after Maghrib, because of the consensus of the people of interpretation on this. And were it not for what you mentioned of their consensus on it, you would have seen that the saying on this matter is what Ibn Zayd said, because God, may He be glorified and exalted, did not specify one prayer with that over another, rather He included the ends of all prayers, so He said:
h
and the ends of prostration

, and there is no proof that it is meant by it the ends of one prayer over another, and there is no proof of acceptance of it from a report or reason. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement:
h
and the ends of prostration
. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Kufa, except for Asim and Al-Kisa’i, recited
h
and the ends of prostration

with a kasra on the alif, as it is the source of adbara idbara. Asim, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Amr recited and the ends with a fatha on the alif, as the plural of dabar and adbar. The correct pronunciation, in my opinion, is the opening of the word dabar.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And listen, O Muhammad, to the shout on the Day of Resurrection, the day when a caller will call out from a nearby place. He said that he calls for it from the rock of Jerusalem.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bishr, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ka’b, who said:
m: h
And listen on the Day when the crier will call from a place nearby
. An angel standing on the rock of Jerusalem will call: O decayed bones and disjointed limbs, God commands you to gather for the passing of judgment.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And listen on the Day when the crier will call from a place nearby
. He said: We were told that he would call from the Holy House from the rock, which is the middle of the earth.

c: Kaab told us:
m: It is the closest land to the sky by eighteen miles.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: On the Day when the crier will call from a nearby place. He said: I have been informed that he will call from the rock in Jerusalem.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And listen on the Day when the crier will call from a place nearby
. He said: It is the shout.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Some of our companions told me, on the authority of Al-Agharr, on the authority of Muslim bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Buraydah, on the authority of his father Buraydah, who said:
m: An angel is standing on the rock of Jerusalem, putting his fingers in his ears, calling out. I said: What is he calling out? He said: He says: O people, come to the accounting. He said: So they come as God said: As if they were locusts scattered (al-Qamar 54:7).

x: And His statement:
h
On the Day they hear the Shout in truth

, God Almighty says: On the Day when creation hears the Shout of Resurrection from the graves in truth, meaning there is no command to respond to God until the place of reckoning. And His saying, That is the Day of Resurrection, means that God Almighty says: The Day when the people of the graves will emerge from their graves.

God Almighty says: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and cause the living to die, and to Us is the destination of all of them on the Day of Resurrection. The Day the earth will split open and reveal them in haste. God Almighty says: And to Us is their destination on the Day the earth will split open. So today is related to destiny.
And his statement:
h
The earth will split open over them
means:
h
The earth will split open over them
. And his statement: Quickly and Quickly is in the accusative case as a state of the ha' and the mim in his statement about them. The meaning is: On the day
h
the earth will split open over them
and they will be destroyed from it quickly. So the indication of his statement:
h
On the day the earth will split open over them was sufficient for mentioning
that. His saying:
h
That is an easy gathering for Us
, means: Their gathering is an easy gathering for Us at the time of reckoning.
God Almighty says: We, O Muhammad, know best what these polytheists say about their slander against God, their denial of His signs, and their denial of God’s ability to resurrect after death.
h
And you are not a tyrant over them
. He says: You are not a power over them.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And you are not a tyrant over them
. He said: Do not be tyrannical toward them.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you are not a tyrant over them

, for God Almighty disliked determinism, forbade it, and presented it in it. Al-Farra’ said: He placed the tyrant in the place of the ruler in determinism, and he said: Al-Mufaddal recited to me: And on the day of sorrow, when Ma'ad was gathered, and the people were all in debt except us. We disobeyed his mighty will until we became the hollow of a thousand teachers It is narrated: Al-Jawf. He said: By Al-Jabbar he meant: Al-Mundhir of his authority. He said: It was said that the meaning of his statement, And you are not a compeller over them is that you were not sent to force them to Islam, rather you were sent as a reminder, so he reminded. He said: The Arabs do not say fa’al from af’alta. They do not say: this is kharaj, meaning exit, nor do they say dakhal, meaning entrance. Rather they say fa’al, from fa’ala, and they say kharaj from kharaja, and dakhal from dakhalat, and qital from qatal. He said: The Arabs say with one letter: daraka, from adarak, and it is anomalous. He said: If you say that the tyrant has this meaning, then it is correct. He said: I heard some Arabs say: He forced him to do something, meaning: He compelled him. So the tyrant in this language is correct, meaning: He subdues them and compels them. And His statement,
h
So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat
, God Almighty says: So remind, O Muhammad, with this Qur’an that I revealed to him whoever fears the threat that I have threatened whoever disobeys Me and opposes My command.

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me: Hakam Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Amr Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: They said, O Messenger of God, if you had frightened us! So the verse was revealed: And remind by the Qur’an whoever fears My threat.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Sayyar Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, who said:
m: They said: O Messenger of God, if you would remind us! So he mentioned something similar.

x: Commentary on Sūrat Qāf. In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

notes.en: Omitted in M. The report appears in Jāmiʿ Maʿmar (no. 20894); through him Muslim transmitted it (no. 2846/34). ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr (2/238), and through him Aḥmad (13/150, no. 7718), from Maʿmar. Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (no. 526) and al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (no. 11522) transmitted it through Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā. Al-Bukhārī (no. 4849), al-Dārimī in al-Radd ʿalā Bishr al-Marīsī, p. 70, Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, pp. 61–62, and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ (no. 6837) transmitted it through Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn. Ibn Abī Shaybah (13/159–160), al-Bukhārī (nos. 4850, 7449), Abū Yaʿlā (no. 6290), Ibn Ḥibbān (no. 7447), al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (no. 331), and others transmitted it through various chains from Abū Hurayrah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (6/107) to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: سقط من: م. والحديث في جامع معمر (20894) - ومن طريقه مسلم (2846/ 34) - وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 238 - وعنه أحمد 13/ 150 (7718) - عن معمر به. وأخرجه ابن أبي عاصم في السنة (526)، والنسائي في الكبرى (11522) عن ابن عبد الأعلى به، وأخرجه البخاري (4849)، والدارمي في الرد على بشر المريسي ص 70، وابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 61، 62، والطبراني في الأوسط (6837) من طريق محمد بن سيرين به وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 159، 160، والبخاري (4850، 7449)، وأبو يعلى (6290)، وابن حبان (7447)، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (331)، وغيرهم من طرق عن أبي هريرة، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 107 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه.
